text: {"frames":["A loud crack echoed up from the canal hall, and the whole Tower seemed to lean. Down by the water, the peat barge had run aground on a hidden sandbank, and its crew sat on the deck with empty stomachs. Sientje-of-the-Dyke climbed down with a warm pizza cut into {a} equal slices, saying it was all she had left from the market. The crew agreed to share it before they pushed the heavy barge free, but they wanted to split the pizza fairly first. How many slices make half of the pizza?","Please, could you help me find my clogs? Wiebe Millsail stood at his bench in the clog maker's room with a wet cloth in his hands and a frown on his face. He had left the clogs by the stove that morning, and now the stove was cold and the clogs were gone. A sharp smell of melted cheese came up from the stairs, where the cheese maker was baking a pizza cut into {a} equal slices. Wiebe promised the cheese maker half the pizza if she found the clogs with him. How many slices make half of the pizza?","The books in the reading room had moved again during the night. Joost Mallemolen found the big atlas on the shelf meant for the fishing tales, and the herbal lay upside down on the window ledge. A small pizza sat on the reading table, its cheese still bubbling, and it had been cut into {a} equal slices by the librarian to share. Joost wanted to give half of it to the book mender, who had spent the whole morning sorting the shelves. How many slices make half of the pizza?","Skates scraped and rang on the ice of the canal below the Tower, and a wild cheer rose from the crowd. The skating race had just ended, and the winners were panting beside the frozen windmill. A tray with a pizza cut into {a} equal slices waited on a wooden crate for them, still warm enough to steam in the cold air. The race judge wanted to hand half of it to the skaters who had come last, so nobody would go home hungry. How many slices make half of the pizza?","Joost Mallemolen slammed a wheel of cheese down on the market stall, and the cheese maker shouted back across the square. The two traders had argued all morning over the price of herring, and now the crowd was pressing close to see who would give way. Trijntje Klomp, who sold waffles beside them, pushed a pizza cut into {a} equal slices across her counter to calm things down. She offered half of it to whichever trader would stop shouting first. How many slices make half of the pizza?"]}
